text:
Elaine: heads-up — ACME reported embeddings perf regression since ~02:00 UTC. tokens/sec looks steady but vectors/sec dropped ~4x.
Omar: any errors coming from their side? auth/billing?
Elaine: they saw a few dimension-mismatch errors in logs: 'expected 1536 got 1024' when calling /v1/embeddings. But most calls are successful; it's only throughput that's tanked.
Sujan: hmm dimension mismatch could cause batching logic to spill. @omar can you pull the worker queue depth for embedding-v2 on us-west-2 around 02:00–03:00?
Omar: grabbing now. infra-bot: alert created: EMBD-QUEUE-LEN high on us-west-2-gpu-pool at 2026-04-11T02:07Z (len=312)
Omar: metrics show queue depth spike correlating with the drop. GPU util hit 96% sustained, per-gpu queue latency jumped.
Elaine: customer said they recently changed client to send variable-length vectors from different models (one 1024-d, one 1536-d) into same endpoint. Could be our batching layer merging incompatible dims.
Jess: do we enforce per-request dim? batching should split by vector size but fallback path might coalesce to generic pipeline and cause re-quantizing -> slower. Any logs showing 'batch compatible' warnings?
Sujan: see snippet from worker logs at 02:06:
```
WARN batching: found mixed-dim requests in batch, falling back to single-stream mode
DEBUG kvcache: eviction pressure high, active_shards=14 pending_ops=48
INFO model: using q4_0 variant for fallback
```
Elaine: that matches. So fallback to single-stream + quantized runtime explains tokens/sec fine (model decode unchanged) but vectors/sec down because embedding postproc now serialized and slower.
Calvin: recommended immediate mitigation: 1) ask ACME to split endpoints by model/dim; 2) implement server-side dimension routing to avoid mixing; 3) short-term we can route their traffic to a dedicated, isolated pool to avoid head-of-line blocking.
Omar: I can create a canary route to dedicated-pool-acme and reroute their traffic. Will enable a small retry/backoff and disable cross-dim batching for that route.
Elaine: can you also gather repro: curl that reproduces mixed-dim batch? i'll test locally.$
Omar: repro curl below (sends two items with different dims):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"input": [["...text..."], ["...other..."]], "model": "embed-multi"}'
```
Elaine: thanks. i'll run against staging with logging on. Jess — can you add a quick metric for 'mixed_dim_fallback_count' and tag by route? we need to quantify how often this happens.
Jess: on it. will push a small telemetry change to include dimension histogram per batch.
Sujan: follow-ups: (a) short term route fix and dedicated pool for ACME; (b) medium term server-side router that partitions batches by dim before batching; (c) longer term validate clients via model registry to avoid accidental mixed requests.
Elaine: i'll update ACME support ticket with repro steps and ETA. thank you all. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy created: route-canary-acme -> dedicated-pool-acme at 2026-04-11T03:10Z by omar
Omar: reroute applied. monitoring shows vectors/sec climbing back after warmup; queue depth dropping to ~40.
Elaine: close loop with ACME after 1h, leaving ticket open until stable.
